llm.summary: This VMware audit and policy skill is mostly coherent, but its documented fail-open and bypass behavior could leave users thinking protections are active when they are not.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose fits the capability: a shared audit logger, policy checker, sanitizer, decorator, and CLI for the VMware skill family. It handles high-impact VMware operations indirectly and stores operational metadata locally, which is expected for audit tooling but sensitive.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill auto-loads across the VMware skill family and documents broad policy bypass and fail-open cases. For a policy-enforcement component, those controls are under-scoped unless users deliberately configure and monitor them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as a uv package, either standalone or as a dependency of other VMware skills. The artifact does not show hidden install steps or unexpected persistence beyond the package and local VMware config directory.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading agent/session-related environment indicators and writing audit data to ~/.vmware/audit.db are purpose-aligned, but the documented VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass and silent allow behavior when rules or PyYAML are absent are risky for production environments.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The local SQLite audit database, WAL mode, log rotation, and ~/.vmware/rules.yaml config are disclosed. The artifact says no network exposure or credential storage, but audit parameters and results may still contain sensitive infrastructure details if redaction is incomplete.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this before installing in production. Create and test ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, install PyYAML, restrict ~/.vmware permissions, monitor for ok_bypassed audit events, and do not rely on this as an enforcement control unless you have verified the rules are active and the bypass environment variable is not set.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad activation through the shared decorator is expected for a family-wide audit and policy layer, but users should understand it becomes part of every VMware skill workflow.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documented VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 behavior is a real policy-control weakness: it bypasses checks across the family and only records the action as bypassed.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit collection of parameters, results, user, agent, workflow, and status is expected for this purpose, but it creates a sensitive local audit store that needs strict file permissions and careful redaction.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Allowing all operations when no rules file exists can be coherent as a default, but it is unsafe for users who install this expecting active policy enforcement.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documented behavior of silently allowing all operations when PyYAML is missing is a material concern because dependency failure disables enforcement without a hard stop.
